newsitem.title: UK: UK-U.S. air cargo rates rise as market strengthens.
newsitem.headline: UK-U.S. air cargo rates rise as market strengthens.

text.p: Air cargo rates from the UK to the United States have strengthened and volumes increased since February after a slow business start to the year, a Reuters survey shows.
Average rates on to the U.S. are expected to go up further over the next few weeks as carriers anxious to offset rising costs, make small but significant rate rises.
Good news for forwarders and shippers is that while basic rates are set to rise, at the same time fuel price surcharges imposed by airlines last November may soon be scrapped.

Already, Delta Air Lines has lifted its 10 U.S. cents per kilo surcharge on all freight shipments between Europe and the U.S. and the U.S.-Asia. Other carriers are likely to follow suit soon, industry observers said.
On ex-UK routes Latin America, rates have generally held firm over the past fortnight, although those to Brazil dipped slightly.

"Our UK-New York bookings, and the size of shipments, have picked up well since the start of 1996 but I can't pinpoint a particular reason why," said Steve Buckerfield, American Airlines' UK cargo sales manager.
"Business from the UK to Chicago, our biggest single U.S. market, has also been very strong of late," he said, adding that British Airways' recent discounting scheme had had no effect on AMR.

SAS's UK/Ireland cargo manager Howard Jones said that while the Scandinavian carrier was only a small niche player in the UK-North America cargo market, it had been maintaining good yields, in particular to Chicago, Seattle, Portland and Vancouver.

Brian Mutton, London-based Atlantic division cargo director of Northwest Airlines, also said his ex-UK business to the U.S. had been strong, since mid-January, but like American, he could not give a reason for this trend.
He noted a healthy growth in UK-manufactured automotive industry-related shipments to Detroit.

"A lot of these components are also made in France, Germany and Spain but, because of the fewer social benefits that have to be provided by employers here, U.S. importers are sometimes finding it cheaper to buy them from Britain," he told Reuters.

Northwest's other ex-UK gateway is Minneapolis, which Mutton described as "a small, niche market that is quite strong and growing for us". Cargo is trucked onward to all other major U.S. destinations.
But while the going was presently good, he warned that Easter is fast approaching and that marked the start of a traditionally slack air cargo period that continued well into May.
"Schools are off, there are holidays all around Europe, production is down...I hate that time of the year," he said.

Kevin Durnin, managing director of London-based Viking Freight Services, also cautioned that current buoyant UK-U.S. business would soon be tempered for another reason -- a huge introduction of extra capacity, mainly on passenger planes, this summer.

Viking purchases space mostly on holiday charter airlines from the UK to Las Vegas, from where it trucks cargo onward to Los Angeles, and to Orlando, which it uses as a transhipment base for Latin America-bound cargo ex-Miami.
"To and from the (U.S.) west coast, our yields have lately been good and have hardened. But we will probably suffer when extra UK-LA capacity is introduced," he said.

Phil Rawlings, Europe cargo sales manager for Air New Zealand, which operates five weekly London Heathrow-Los Angeles-Auckland 747-400 passenger flights offering a total 35 tonnes' capacity, described the UK-California airfreight market as "totally unpredictable".

"It appears to me, and to other airlines on the route I've spoken to, that at the beginning of each month, business is bad. It certainly was dire for us at the start of March but now, halfway through the month, we are fully booked," he said.
"This trend has been apparent since 1995. Why, I don't know. It could well be local production manufacturing patterns. But it does mean that we can't plan ahead," he said.

ANZ's UK-Los Angeles airfreight mainly comprised lighter-weight shipments including clothing, fabrics, car spares, pop group equipment and exhibition and promotional material, plus occasional heavier pieces such as racing car engines.
"It is a highly competitive route," he said, a sentiment echoed by Viking's Durnin, who said he faces even fiercer battle for business to Florida from May.

Extra capacity would be provided by an upsurge in ex-UK flights to Orlando provided not only by Leisure International who is Viking's main carrier, but also from Britannia Airways, Airtours, Caledonian, Laker, Delta Air Lines, Virgin and BA.

"In the summer, this cargo market goes crazy. Our rates now are, for us, fine but the danger is that some customers may go for cheap rates resulting from all the extra capacity that will become available rather than quality of service. This is what happened last summer, when rates fell by 20 percent," he said.
Key U.S. routes subject to discounting based on UK-Orlando flights included Dallas, Houston, New Orleans, Atlanta, Raleigh-Durham, Charlotte and Miami, all within easy trucking reach.

As a precaution against "another downward rates spiral", Durnin is placing increasing emphasis on ex-UK interine services to Latin America via Miami, from where he said he had agreements with Fine Air, Challenge Air Cargo, Tampa Airlines, COPA, Arow Air, Millon Airlines and TACA.
"Our business to South and Central America has been going very well, with Chile being our top market followed by Uruguay, Peru, Colombia and Venezuela," he noted.
There is still a big shortage of airfreight capacity on ex-UK routes to Latin America, whether or not they are offered direct or via transhipment points, industry.

"This is true, and so people are paying premium rates for LAN-Chile's services, which we believe are of quality standard," said Steve Dawkins, of the carrier's UK cargo general sales agent Air Logistics.

His company trucks cargo from Britain each night for loading on LAN-Chile's five-weekly, 12-tonne cargo capacity Boeing 767-300ER Frankfurt-Santiago passenger services and a weekly 38-tonne DC-8 freighter flight from Luxembourg to the Chile capital.
Onward connectons are provided to Montevideo, Sao Paulo and Buenos Aires, amongst other South American destinations.

"Air cargo business from Europe as a whole to South America is currently very buoyant. The market there is really opening up, notably for automobile spares and agricultural equipment made in the UK," he said.
Lufthansa Cargo's UK/Ireland marketing manager Ruediger Helm said its small Latin American market, it was rapidly growing.
"This is particularly the case with Brazil. We got some good business to both Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro last year, much more than in 1995, and Brazil continues to develop for us," he said.
Varig's UK cargo manager Paul Ryan described the UK-Brazil market as "still fairly buoyant, and we are currently very busy".
Ryan has no immediate plans to match BA's 10 percent rise in UK-South America rates from March 17. "We'll have a look at the situation in April," he added.
BA will on March 17 transfer its routes to Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Chile, Mexico and Venezuela to London Gatwick from Heathrow. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+ 44 171 547 7706; fax +5017
